raw.assessment: The incumbent combines printed access, a common topic and a predictable practice sequence. Seven frequent attendees explicitly valued the repeated structure, supporting retention of that scaffold, although its causal contribution is unmeasured. The concrete limiting observation is that five occasional attendees struggled to enter conversations already familiar to partners (H3-O6): structural familiarity may help some without providing a shared conversational starting point for others. Pair delays and changes are compatible with that account but do not establish it. Across 72 slips, 49 reported ten useful minutes and 48 identified the intended task; these fall below the targets among respondents, while missing slips from 97 attendances prevent a complete attendance-level assessment. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Supplied observations are synthetic; the proposed explanations remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with the conversation, rather than unfamiliarity with the session sequence alone, may impede occasional attendees' entry into useful practice.
openings.delta: Retain the familiar sequence but start paired practice with a self-contained current-session prompt that requires no earlier conversation or preparation.
openings.prediction: Compared with usual prompts, self-contained prompts reduce stalled starts and early partner changes, particularly in pairs reporting unequal topic familiarity. No differential improvement would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Within existing paired time, counterbalance matched self-contained and usual prompts across pairs. Observe start delays and each partner's speaking time; collect anonymous topic-familiarity and usefulness responses without public proficiency labels. Include everyone regardless of prior attendance and record volunteer preparation time.
assumptions: Matched prompts can differ in dependence on prior conversation without materially differing in difficulty.
Observation and prompt adaptation fit existing volunteer time; this requires measurement.

openings.claim: Confusion between earlier and next preparation tasks may partly reflect weak temporal cues on printed information.
openings.delta: Add a prominent session date and one explicitly labeled next-session preparation box to the existing printed sheet.
openings.prediction: With identical task content, clearer temporal cues reduce earlier-task answers. Persistent blank answers despite fewer earlier-task answers would suggest an additional access or comprehension problem.
openings.probe: Distribute usual and clearly dated versions of the same sheet within sessions and compare anonymous next-task identification at exit, recording which version was received. Keep printed copies available during the weekly session and participation independent of preparation; log printing and clarification time against the 90-minute ceiling.
assumptions: Temporal cue confusion contributes to some earlier-task answers; current sheet wording is not supplied.
Improved immediate identification may not persist until the next attendance.

raw.assessment: The observations suggest entry and preparation difficulties but establish neither their causes nor individual proficiency mismatch. Useful practice is self-reported; missing slips and answers prevent a complete attendee-level baseline. The capabilities below are hypotheses, with success judged against all three stipulated six-session measures.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: a paper conversation kit lets an unfamiliar pair start a mutually useful exchange without shared attendance history or public proficiency labels. Each independent scenario supplies a common opening, optional private phrase support, an optional elaboration challenge, and alternating speaker roles.
openings.delta: Replace dependence on a partner's prior conversation context with a reusable, self-contained starting point while retaining the familiar session structure.
openings.prediction: Pairs using the kit start substantive exchanges sooner and show fewer early partner changes; participants using different supports still report useful practice. Faster starts without increased usefulness would weaken the proposed mechanism.
openings.probe: Dependencies are understandable scenarios, supports that serve different needs without assigning labels, balanced turns, and cheap reuse. Test the partial capability using two existing topics and two short rounds, alternating kit order across pairs. An anonymous observer records start delay, speaker time and partner changes; brief slips separately assess usefulness. Log preparation effort before extending to six sessions.
assumptions: Support choices can remain private within ordinary printed sheets.
A common opening can accommodate materially different conversational needs.
Reusable kits can fit existing printing and volunteer time.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: a printed, date-addressed six-session preparation map allows someone returning after absences to recover the correct task without asking a volunteer.
openings.delta: Address each independent preparation task by Wednesday date rather than by a sequence learners must remember or complete.
openings.prediction: When given hypothetical return dates, readers choose fewer earlier tasks from a dated map than from current sheets. No improvement would weaken date ambiguity as an explanation for task errors.
openings.probe: Dependencies are advance topic commitments, legible dates, independent conversational tasks and replacement copies. Test the partial capability with a three-date paper prototype, counterbalancing format order and asking readers to explain the selected task. Separately record task selection errors and comprehension errors; then measure weekly update effort before expanding.
assumptions: Topics can be committed sufficiently early.
Participants can retain a paper map; replacement copies are available at sessions.
Task selection contributes to observed preparation errors.

openings.claim: Unequal conversational familiarity may obstruct entry despite a helpful familiar sequence.
openings.discriminator: Self-contained prompts particularly improve unequal-familiarity pairs.
openings.fit: Preserves sequence and inclusive conversational practice.
openings.probe: Counterbalance matched usual/self-contained prompts; observe starts, speaker time, partner changes; privately assess familiarity/usefulness and log effort.
openings.uncertainty: Prompt difficulty matching and volunteer capacity unproven.

openings.claim: Reusable independent paper scenarios with private phrase support, elaboration challenges and alternating roles may accommodate differing needs.
openings.discriminator: Faster starts must also increase usefulness across support choices.
openings.fit: Preserves sequence, participation and label privacy.
openings.probe: Two topics, two rounds, counterbalanced kit order; observe starts, speaking time and changes; collect usefulness and preparation effort.
openings.uncertainty: Support privacy, common-opening suitability, balanced turns and economical reuse unproven.

openings.claim: Prominent dates and a next-task box may correct temporal confusion.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors fall; persistent blanks suggest access/comprehension issues.
openings.fit: Preserves printed access and optional preparation.
openings.probe: Compare identical content on usual/dated sheets using exit task identification; log printing/clarification time.
openings.uncertainty: Current wording unknown; immediate recall may not persist.

openings.claim: A dated multi-session paper map may enable independent task recovery after absence.
openings.discriminator: Hypothetical return-date selection improves; separate selection from comprehension errors.
openings.fit: Preserves independent conversational tasks and offline access.
openings.probe: Counterbalance three-date prototype/current sheets; request task explanations; measure update effort before expansion.
openings.uncertainty: Advance commitments, paper retention and replacement copies required.

lineage.reason: Adds differentiated support and turn allocation.

post_distill.decision: Probe before adoption. All remain free, exclude nobody for absence or withheld labels, retain offline information and conversational purpose, and fit one room/75 minutes without paid time. Synthetic, incomplete self-reports establish no cause. Evaluate six-session targets: 80% useful speaking, 85% preparation identification, coordination below 90 minutes weekly.
